title: 58 Pilot: Tag weight capacity of cattle ears
content:
Abstract
The objective of this pilot study was to measure the effect of tag weight on damage to cattle ears. Precision livestock management technology often assumes an ear tag form factor for convenience, but heavy sensor tags may not be tolerated well by cattle. Typical plastic ear tags weigh approximately 15 g; however commercial sensor tags can weigh up to 60 g, and can stretch the tag puncture site leading to potential cattle welfare problems in addition to loss of the sensor and data. A series of three experiments were conducted at the Oklahoma State University Bluestem Research Range with weaned calves. In each experiment, animals were tagged with a commercial plastic ear tag with varying amounts of steel weight added (automotive wheel weights adhered to the back of the tag). Tags were removed on 14 or 28-d intervals and the puncture diameter was measured with calipers. Tags were then reattached in the same puncture site to continue the experiment. Experiments ranged from 28 to 84 days in length. Experiments included 15 to 38 cattle each (steers and heifers 119 to 350 kg), and tag weights ranging from 15 to 92 g. In one experiment, weighted tags were applied in both fresh punctures and also in puncture sites that had been allowed to heal for 28 d with an unweighted tag. Puncture site diameter data were analyzed with regression in R with tag weight, day, puncture healing status, and animal BW as independent variables. The model explained 54% of puncture site diameter variation. For reference, puncture diameter immediately after tag application was 6.5 mm, and had stretched to 15.1 mm after 30 d with a 30-g tag. Healed punctures resisted stretching better than unhealed punctures (9 mm less puncture stretch, P < 0.01). Heavier tags increased puncture diameter over time (P < 0.01), with no clear threshold effect, indicating that lighter tags may always be preferable. Larger animals tended (P = 0.07) tended to tolerate heavier tags slightly better (0.03 mm less puncture stretch per kg of BW). Additional research is necessary to generate sensor tag weight guidelines.
